root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before cleanup re-enters `Curl_pp_readresp()` on the rebound closure handle, `Curl_conncache_close_all_connections()` must provide a receive buffer whose actual extent is at least `conn->data->set.buffer_size + 1`, because the cached IMAP replay path later accepts that many bytes.
root_cause_criterion.description: In the vulnerable original the rebound closure handle reaches this point with `sizeof(buffer) = 1024` and `conn->data->set.buffer_size + 1 = 1025`, so the required slack byte is missing while the protected IMAP cached-copy `memcpy` still executes. In the fixed original the same source-level contract is satisfied (`1025 >= 1025`) and the protected `memcpy` executes on the repaired buffer.

nodes.description: At the AddressSanitizer sink, `memcpy(ptr, pp->cache, pp->cache_size)` copies the cached IMAP response tail into the rebound closure-handle receive buffer.

edges.relation: After cleanup rebinds the live connection to the closure handle, the same `conn->data->state.buffer` pointer is later passed as the `ptr` destination argument to the cached-copy `memcpy`.
The cached IMAP response tail already queued on the live connection remains the same `pp->cache` source pointer later consumed by `memcpy`.
The queued IMAP cached-tail length remains the same `pp->cache_size` byte count later used as the `memcpy` length.
